gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-chivo: Heavy and bent-straw bold, Plakkaat draws curls that nearly close back onto the stem, while Chivo keeps daylight showing through every curve. One shouts in tight shapes; the other talks in open ones.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-chocolate-classic: Chocolate Classical Sans carries a sizable lowercase drawn with a broad-nibbed pen that never curls shut, a loose, friendly hand under Plakkaat's stiff headlines. And the ribbon-cut constant width of Plakkaat against that open pen stroke is what makes the pair memorable.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-comme: Plakkaat's terminals curl round until they nearly touch the stem. Make that heading small and its closed, heavy shapes crowd together, while Comme, a sans with lowercase filling most of the letter height, only starts to feel natural when it is large.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-cossette-texte: Cossette Texte feels clean and unfussy, with wide-eyed e shapes and a prominent x-height under Plakkaat's heavy bent-straw lines. But where the heading closes its curves tight, this plain sans keeps arches as thick as its stems, easing a long page along.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-duru-sans: Plakkaat's lines never swell or thin, like a bent straw. Duru Sans answers with wide openings on small letters and bodies that dominate the line, so a long stretch of it reads smoothly, with ascenders barely poking up.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-fresca: Modern and clean at the body end, this pairing starts with Plakkaat's heavy, bent-straw capitals and closed curls. Fresca keeps its counters connected to the space outside, and that open-versus-shut tension is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-funnel-sans: Funnel Sans has an e opened like a pried clasp and tiny gaps between ascender tops and the x-height line, which looks sharp beside Plakkaat's heavy shapes. Plakkaat is best at closing its curls tight around the stem, while Funnel Sans is best at staying open and consistent from stem to curve.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-gafata: Gafata sets a tall band of letters with short stalks above and a wide-eyed e, a professional sans-serif voice. But Plakkaat earns its keep big and brief, where its heavy, closed, uniform strokes can hit hard.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-geist: Plakkaat comes in heavy, with bent-straw lines and curled terminals that nearly touch the stem. And Geist lets a quiet, level sans follow with an opening like a sprung paper clip, so words form solid blocks under the shouting.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-georama: Plakkaat is heavy and bent-straw bold, its curled terminals closing almost to the stem, while Georama opens its c like a bracelet pulled apart. That tight-against-open tension is the pair's best trait.
